title: Stability Standup Snapshot - 2026-09-24
content:
Summary:
- Short recap: partial degradation of hosted inference in eu-west-1 during morning traffic spike (09:12-09:37 UTC). Root cause appears related to cascading cache eviction under a hot-prefix workload and an autoscaler race condition on behind-the-scenes pool managers.

Incident highlights:
- Severity: P1 degraded latency for ~25% of requests to model 'redwood-mini-3b'.
- Impact window: 2026-09-24T09:12Z to 2026-09-24T09:37Z (25 min).
- Observed symptoms: token latency tail spiking to 2.1s (p50: 120ms baseline), increased 429s from cache-miss burst, autoscale up/down churn recorded in control-plane logs.
- Quick mitigation applied: throttled burst traffic via rate-limit override (09:16), pin-fallback to quantized variant 'rmini-3b-q4' for high-latency routes (09:20), manual pause of aggressive autoscale policy (09:24).

Timeline (high level):
- 09:12: first latency anomaly alerted by SLO monitor (p95 > 700ms).
- 09:14: oncall paged (paging playbook: SRE-P1-eviction).
- 09:16: initial mitigation — soft rate-limit enacted for tenant-heavy route (team decision: hold traffic to 60%).
- 09:20: rollback to q4 variant for worst-affected route via route policy; immediate token-latency improvement starts.
- 09:24: localized autoscaler observed churning; manual intervention issued to disable scale-down for 10m.
- 09:30: p95 under 350ms; incident declared contained at 09:37.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Primary: prefix/KV cache eviction cascade interacting poorly with a recent change in the pool manager's scale-down window (PR #742). Hot-prefix workload caused cache pressure leading to sudden miss spike.
- Secondary: autoscaler churn amplified tail latencies because new nodes joined but KV warming lagged, and aggressive scale-down immediately removed warmed instances.

Monitoring & telemetry notes:
- Missing metric: per-pool KV warmup latency (filed as SRE-914) — we only have node-level metrics; need per-model/pool detail.
- Suggested dashboard updates: add a 'kv-warmth' heatmap and a per-route cache hit/miss timeseries (for quick triage).

SLO snapshot (pre/post incident):
- Model-serving p95 SLO (monthly): 99.0% (target >= 99.5%).
- Today pre-incident: 99.45% for rolling 7d, during incident dropped to 98.7% for the 1h window.
- Error budget: remaining monthly budget ~0.9% — this incident consumed ~0.35%.

On-call handoff notes (for next shift):
- Follow-up tasks prioritized in action-items; handoff owner: Miguel Ortiz.
- Key watchpoints: kv-cache miss ratio per pool, autoscale scale-down events, route-policy fallbacks triggered.
- Contact list: infra-pool-owner (lina@redwood.ai), runtime-owner (tom@redwood.ai), model-oncall (ml-oncall@redwood.ai).

Action items (owner — ETA — status):
- Add 'kv-warmth' metric and dashboard (Miguel Ortiz — 2026-09-30 — open).
- Back out scale-down tweak in PR #742 or tune window (Tomáš Novak — 2026-09-26 — in_progress).
- Postmortem draft with timeline and RCA (Aisha Patel — 2026-09-28 — open).
- Create runbook: hot-prefix mitigation play (Lina Chen — 2026-10-04 — open).
- Add canary test to detect KV-eviction cascades during autoscale events (infra eng — 2026-10-10 — planned).

Notes & loose thoughts (notes-to-self style):
- Repro: need to replay tenant workload with large prefix overlap; riff on synthetic traffic generator used in serving runtime tests.
- Consider temporary hard quota per-tenant for prefix-cache memory until we have finer warming heuristics.
- Evaluate whether the control plane should stagger scale-downs to allow KV warming per model.

References & links:
- JIRA: SRE-914 (kv metric), SRE-915 (postmortem), INFRA-827 (autoscaler policy change), SRE-916 (runbook).
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/742
- Slack thread: #sre-incident-eu-west1 (link in linked_artifacts)

Open questions for next call:
- How much of the SLO hit is correlated to a small set of tenants vs broad traffic? (Data check: top 10 tenants by request during window)
- Do we have a low-risk way to warm KV cache across new nodes faster without violating isolation constraints?

Quick wins to reduce blast radius:
- Implement short-term per-tenant prefix memory caps (config flag) — low effort.
- Lower aggressiveness of scale-down policy during peak hours (experiment: reduce scale-down rate by 50% for 7d).

Last-minute operational notes:
- Incident has been escalated to ENG leadership; no customer-facing incident page published yet — CS notified to prepare comms if needed.
- Handing over to night shift with watchlist in the action-items; if p95 rises >500ms again, escalate to paged-oncall immediately.

Rough scratch area:
- TODO: capture sample trace ids (saved in S3: s3://redwood-ops/incident-2026-09-24/traces)
- TODO: attach ASG logs; control-plane trace id: cp-ff7a6

End of note.
